dimension: Open-source river routing, hydraulics and 2D flood inundation (adversarial verification pass)

confirmed_sources.name: CWC River Water Level (Manual - Hourly), basin 031 - India National Water Data Portal
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Hourly manual river stage + reservoir level CSVs by BASIN code. I re-downloaded nothing but independently re-parsed both cached files with my own script: wl031.csv = 1,284,651 rows spanning 1991-01-01..2020-12-31; wl031b.csv = 1,139,984 rows spanning 2021-01-01..2025-12-31. Every claimed per-station row count matched EXACTLY: NEELEESWARAM 31,172+25,643; ARANGALI 30,186+27,460; VANDIPERIYAR 48,949+26,714; Idukki (Eb)/Idukki Arch Reservoir 3,532+9,477; Idamalayar Reservoir 3,621+9,561. Aug-2018 stage at NEELEESWARAM confirmed value-for-value: 6.12 m at 2018-08-14 00:00 rising to 12.40 m first reached 2018-08-16 16:00. Reservoir spot-checks confirmed exactly: Idukki 722.31 m @2020-08-13 01:00, 728.69 m @2021-10-15 01:00; Idamalayar 152.58 m and 164.23 m at the same stamps.
confirmed_sources.relevance: HIGHEST. Genuinely closes gap #1 (no pre-2020 Periyar data) for river stage. Provides an independent reservoir-level record starting 2019-06-10, 14 months before amith-vp.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: partly - all NUMBERS verified exact, but the routing INTERPRETATION is wrong. See caveat.
confirmed_sources.caveat: THREE material corrections. (1) ARANGALI IS NOT ON THE PERIYAR. The file's own metadata says Tributary=Chalakudy, Local River=Chalakudy, District=THRISSUR. The 'River=Periyar' column is a basin-group label, not the watercourse. So NEELEESWARAM+ARANGALI are NOT an inflow->outflow pair and cannot be used for a Muskingum K/x fit. The only two true Periyar-mainstem gauges are VANDIPERIYAR (9.573N,77.091E) and NEELEESWARAM (10.184N,76.496E) - and Mullaperiyar's inter-basin diversion, Idukki and Idamalayar all sit between them, so that pair is not an unregulated reach either. (2) RESERVOIR GAP: the series runs 2019-06-10..2020-12-31 then jumps to 2021-05-12. It covers only 2020-09-25..2020-12-31 of the amith-vp corrupt window (881 readings, last 2020-12-31 22:00) and misses ALL of 2021-01-01..2021-04-30. It repairs roughly 44%% of the corrupt window, not the whole of it. (3) STAGE IS SEASONAL, not continuous hourly: NEELEESWARAM 2018 monthly completeness is Aug 100%%, Jul 98%%, Oct 89%%, Sep 87%%, Jun 84%%, Nov 69%%, but only 11-15%% Dec-May. Also 1,337 duplicated timestamps in the 1991-2020 file, 667 of them carrying CONFLICTING values - dedupe before use. Reservoir rows include a few physically impossible values (Idukki max 7222.19 m, Idamalayar max 1621.1 m) but corruption is small: 99.8-100%% fall in plausible bands.
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Direct CSV, no auth. Resource names follow rwl_manual_hr_cwc_031_1991_2020.csv / _2021_2025.csv. The dataset page lists 88 resources total and ALSO carries basin-031 files for 1961-1990 and 2026-2030 that the prior sweep did not mention - worth checking for more pre-2020 data.
confirmed_sources.license: page does not print a licence string in the fetched view; portal-wide terms are 'Other (Open)'

confirmed_sources.name: CWC River Discharge (Manual - Daily), Kerala
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Daily gauged discharge. Independently re-parsed the cached 2001-2025 Kerala file: 217,538 rows, 40 distinct stations - both EXACT matches. NEELEESWARAM (River=Periyar, Local River=Periyar) has 8,478 values 2001-01-01..2025-12-31. Record max 6,323.5474 m3/s on 2013-08-05 (exact). 2018-08-15 = 6,166.426 (exact). October 2021 case study fully covered: 2021-10-09 = 695.46, 2021-10-12 = 1,387.14 (both exact). ARANGALI 7,518 rows, VANDIPERIYAR 14,837 rows - both exact.
confirmed_sources.relevance: HIGH. The discharge half of the rating-curve route, and an independent check on the Oct-2021 flagship replay.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes - every single figure reproduced exactly from my own parse
confirmed_sources.caveat: The 7-day hole is REAL and I confirmed it precisely: 2018-08-16 through 2018-08-22 are all absent, next value is 2018-08-23 = 924.282. Note 2018-08-24 is also missing. So the flood peak is genuinely not in the public daily series, exactly as claimed.
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Direct CSV per state per epoch; Kerala 2001-2025 is 39.4 MB

confirmed_sources.name: CWC Study Report: Kerala Floods of August 2018 (Hydrology (S) Dte)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: I read the extracted text directly. Confirmed VERBATIM: contents list has '4.1 Runoff computations of Periyar sub-basin', '4.1.1 Reservoir operation of Idukki', '4.1.2 Reservoir operation of Idamalayar'. Quote: 'The Periyar river has a drainage area of 4,033 sq km upto CWC gauging station at Neeleshwaram.' Mullaperiyar 637 sq.km, Idukki free catchment 605 sq.km, Idamalayar 472 sq.km - all present. Idukki narrative verbatim: 731.82 m at 10 Aug 00:00, '0.61 m below FRL', cushion 'about 40 MCM'; spill raised to '750 cumec (plus 118 cumec power house release) by 17:00 hrs on 10 August 2018'; level 'dropped to 730.80 m increasing the extra flood cushion below FRL to about 90 MCM'; 'peak inflow of about 2532 cumec into dam occurred at 22:00 hrs on 15 August 2018'; 'attenuated from 2532 cumec to 1500 cumec (an attenuation of about 41%% downstream of Idukki)'; 'reservoir touched FRL of 732.43 m at 01:00 hrs on 17 August 2018'. And 'a flood peak of about 8800 cumec was observed at Neeleswaram G&D site'.
confirmed_sources.relevance: HIGHEST for the 2018 gap. Supplies the dam-outflow boundary condition that the CWC gauge data lacks, and independently corroborates AquaSync's own constants.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes - every claimed figure found verbatim in the report text
confirmed_sources.caveat: Bonus cross-validation the prior sweep missed: the report states Idukki gross storage 1997 MCM at FRL 732.43 m, MDDL 694.94 m, and 'live storage between FRL and MDDL is about 1460 MCM' - which corroborates AquaSync's 1459 Mm3 to within 0.1%%. Caution: the '8800 cumec at 14:00 on 16 Aug' TIMING is read off Fig.3, not stated in the text; the text gives only the magnitude. That magnitude also exceeds the entire public daily record (max 6,323 in 2013), so treat 8,800 as report-derived, not gauge-derived.

confirmed_sources.name: Deltares/SFINCS (+ hydromt_sfincs)
confirmed_sources.kind: GitHub repo (Fortran solver) + Python model builder
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Reduced-complexity 2D compound-flood solver. SFINCS docs confirm the variant naming VERBATIM: 'Traditionally SFINCS neglects the advection term (SFINCS-LIE) which generally justified for sub-critical flow conditions. For super-critical flow conditions or when modelling waves, the advection term needs to be solved. For this purpose, the SFINCS-SSWE version can be used'. README confirms compound flooding across 'fluvial, pluvial, tidal, wind- and wave-driven processes', and the docs reference discharge points with time-series, downstream water-level time-series boundaries, and local rainfall - i.e. AquaSync's three forcings. Companion hydromt_sfincs takes you 'from raw data to a complete model instance which is ready to run'.
confirmed_sources.relevance: HIGHEST for gap #4 (2D inundation). Only candidate needing no Fortran compiler and no week of DEM conditioning.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes - LIE/SSWE naming confirmed verbatim in docs; forcings confirmed; distribution channels confirmed
confirmed_sources.caveat: Licence is split and the prior sweep glossed it: SOURCE is GPL-3.0, but the precompiled Windows executable ships under the Deltares Freeware licence with 'no distribution, no modification'. If AquaSync is to be handed to KSEB/KSDMA, that distinction matters. Subgrid bathymetry is real but I could not confirm it from the README or the overview page - it lives deeper in the manual.
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Windows exe: https://download.deltares.nl/sfincs ; Linux/Mac/HPC: docker pull deltares/sfincs-cpu ; builder: pip install hydromt-sfincs
confirmed_sources.last_activity: SFINCS pushed 2026-08-24, release v2.4.0_Galibier_release 2026-06-15; hydromt_sfincs pushed 2026-08-18, PyPI 1.2.2 on 2025-12-02

confirmed_sources.name: NOAA-OWP/t-route
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Muskingum-Cunge and diffusive-wave routing. README confirms the parallelism split verbatim: MC is 'Parallel on CONUS using junction order and short-time step', diffusive is 'Serial on a sub-network using junction order'. Supports NHDNetwork or HYFeatures; BMI supports HYFeatures only.
confirmed_sources.relevance: LOW-MEDIUM. AquaSync already has Muskingum with sub-reaching. The prior sweep's own 'not worth it' verdict is correct and I confirmed the evidence behind it.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes - including the unflattering parts
confirmed_sources.caveat: The staleness call checks out and is if anything understated. GitHub pushed_at is 2026-08-18 but the last commit ON master is 2025-01-31 ('Updated license file to reflect OWP government language') and the last tagged release is v2.4.0 from 2024-10-02. README concedes verbatim: 'While the code is currently bespoke for NWM, efforts are ongoing to generalize the core utilities.' Build needs gcc-gfortran + netcdf-fortran (4.6.1 in the example) + compiler.sh, and README states 'If you are using Windows, please install WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) before proceeding.'
confirmed_sources.last_activity: pushed_at 2026-08-18 but master last commit 2025-01-31; last release v2.4.0 2024-10-02

confirmed_sources.name: rileyhales/river-route
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Vectorised Muskingum-family routing on vector stream networks. Three routers confirmed: Muskingum ('Channel routing only (no lateral inflow)'), RapidMuskingum, UnitMuskingum. Uses 'numba-compiled kernels and sparse matrix operations'. The params-file spec is confirmed VERBATIM from docs/references/io-file-schema.md: a parquet, one row per river, with exactly river_id (integer), downstream_river_id (integer, '-1 for outlet reaches'), k (float), x (float, 'expected in [0, 0.5]'), and a warning that rows 'must be sorted in topological order from upstream to downstream'.
confirmed_sources.relevance: MEDIUM. Good short reference implementation of sparse-matrix Muskingum; not a calibrator.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes - the four-column parquet spec matched word for word
confirmed_sources.caveat: No calibration module, confirmed: the docs say k and x come 'from hydraulic assumptions and/or calibration' performed elsewhere. Only 4 stars. Requires Python >=3.12, which may not match AquaSync's environment.

confirmed_sources.name: LISFLOOD-FP 8.x (SEAMLESS-WAVE / Sheffield)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Canonical academic 2D floodplain code. Page confirms DG2/FV1 solvers, GPU-accelerated ACC solvers, versions 8.1 and 8.2, a GPU multiwavelet DG2 solver with dynamic adaptivity (GPU-MWDG2), a DG2-RANS solver, and 'LISFLOOD-FP 8.0 is cross-platform and can be compiled on Windows or Linux using CMake version 3.13 or above'.
confirmed_sources.relevance: MEDIUM. Heavier route to gap #4 than SFINCS; the prior sweep's 2-4 weeks vs 2-4 days comparison is a fair characterisation.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes
confirmed_sources.caveat: I chased the citation because it looked hallucination-shaped and it is NOT: https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/18/9827/2025/ resolves 200 and is 'LISFLOOD-FP 8.2: GPU-accelerated multiwavelet discontinuous Galerkin solver with dynamic resolution adaptivity for rapid, multiscale flood simulation', Chowdhury & Kesserwani, GMD 18(23), 9827-9854, 10 Dec 2025. Worth noting the seamlesswave page itself cites a DIFFERENT paper (Kesserwani et al. 2025, Advances in Water Resources 201C, 104986) - both are real, so cite deliberately.

confirmed_sources.name: Deltares/pyflwdir
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Pure-Python numba-accelerated terrain/hydrography analysis. Docs list confirmed VERBATIM: 'flow directions from elevation data using a steepest gradient algorithm / strahler stream order / flow direction upscaling / (sub)basin delineation / pfafstetter subbasins delineation / classic stream order / height above nearest drainage (HAND) / geomorphic floodplain delineation / up- and downstream tracing and arithmetics / hydrologically adjusting elevation / upstream accumulation / vectorizing streams'.
confirmed_sources.relevance: HIGH. The practical way to get HAND and a conditioned DEM for the Aluva reach without a compiler; also the DEM-conditioning step SFINCS needs.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes - the full feature list matched item for item, including HAND and floodplain delineation

confirmed_sources.name: Deltares/hydromt_sfincs
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Python plugin that automates SFINCS model building, described as tools 'to go from raw data to a complete model instance which is ready to run and to analyse model results'. Usable as a CLI driven by config files, or directly from Python.
confirmed_sources.relevance: HIGH. This is what makes the SFINCS route a 2-4 day job rather than a schematisation slog.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: partly - the build-from-config workflow is confirmed, but the specific 'YAML data catalogue plus an INI' phrasing and the individual steps (grid setup, subgrid tables, bathymetry merging, forcing) are not spelled out on the repo landing page

confirmed_sources.name: gpt-cmdr/ras-commander
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Python API for HEC-RAS 6.x. Confirmed: 'Parallel Execution of Multiple Plans' via RasCmdr.compute_parallel(); standalone HDF result reading without HEC-RAS installed; an HdfResultsMesh class doing '2D mesh results processing (depths, velocities, WSE)'; and the function 'HdfResultsMesh.export_max_depth_raster()' is explicitly listed.

confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes - HdfResultsMesh and export_max_depth_raster() both confirmed by name

confirmed_sources.name: psu-efd/pyHMT2D
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Control and semi-automation of 2D hydraulic models with pre/post-processing: edit Manning's n and boundary conditions, run 'batch simulations to calibrate model runs', Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis, convert results to VTK, extract cross-sections and flood extents, convert HEC-RAS meshes to SRH-2D format.
confirmed_sources.relevance: MEDIUM. The batch-calibration and Monte Carlo machinery is the interesting part for AquaSync, not the model control.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: partly - SRH-2D and HEC-RAS 2D confirmed, but Backwater-1D is documented as 'a demonstration toy model', not a production solver as the phrasing 'Supports SRH-2D, HEC-RAS and Backwater-1D' implies
confirmed_sources.caveat: Requires the external software (SRH-2D via SMS, and/or HEC-RAS) to be installed separately - it is a driver, not a solver. Given HEC-RAS is Windows-only and its download host is unreachable from this network, that is a real blocker here.

confirmed_sources.name: Landlab (OverlandFlow component)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: OverlandFlow implements the de Almeida et al. (2012) local-inertial approximation of the 2D shallow water equations on a raster grid. Component citation confirmed: Adams et al. (2017), 'The Landlab v1.0 OverlandFlow component: a Python tool for computing shallow-water flow across watersheds', Geoscientific Model Development 10(4), 1645.
confirmed_sources.relevance: MEDIUM. A pip-installable 2D local-inertial solver - the same physics family as SFINCS-LIE - useful as a cross-check or a fast prototype before committing to SFINCS.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: partly - de Almeida 2012 physics and the GMD 10/1645/2017 citation confirmed exactly; but the documented output fields are surface water depth (nodes), surface water discharge (links) and water surface gradient (links). Shear stress is mentioned but is not one of the primary output fields, so 'returning depth, discharge and shear stress' overstates it slightly.

confirmed_sources.name: MERIT Hydro / MERIT DEM
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 90 m (3 arc-second) globally consistent hydrography on the error-corrected MERIT DEM, 90N-60S, 5x5 degree GeoTIFF tiles. Six layers confirmed: flow direction, upstream drainage area, upstream gradient, river channel width, hydrologically adjusted elevation, and HAND. Page states it is 'designed for global to regional hydrodynamic and flood simulations'.
confirmed_sources.relevance: HIGH. The conditioned-DEM and HAND base layer for any 2D or HAND-based work on the Periyar, and the substrate MERIT-Basins is built from.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes - though note the layer is 'upstream drainage area', which is flow accumulation expressed as area rather than a separate accumulation grid
confirmed_sources.caveat: LICENCE OMITTED BY THE PRIOR SWEEP and it is restrictive: dual-licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial) OR ODbL 1.0 (commercial use allowed but derived data must be released publicly under ODbL share-alike). Redistribution of the data in its original format needs written author permission. For a KSEB/KSDMA deployment this is a decision point, not a footnote.

confirmed_sources.name: MERIT-Basins (reachhydro.org)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 'A global vector hydrography database derived from the 90-m MERIT-Hydro product using the TauDEM tool.' ~2.94M river reaches plus unit catchments. File naming confirmed: riv_pfaf_XX_MERIT_Hydro_v07_Basins_v01.shp and cat_pfaf_XX_MERIT_Hydro_v07_Basins_v01.shp. Attributes confirmed: lengthkm, slope, uparea, Strahler order, NextDownID, maxup, up1-up4. Pfafstetter level-1 zone 4 = South Asia.
confirmed_sources.relevance: HIGH. This is the object that settles the Periyar/Chalakudy reach topology and supplies the river_id/downstream_river_id/k/x skeleton river-route wants.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes - naming convention, attribute list, reach count and pfaf zone 4 all confirmed

confirmed_sources.name: GRFR - Global Reach-level Flood Reanalysis
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: VIC land-surface model coupled to RAPID routing. 3-hourly and daily river discharge for the same 2.94M MERIT-Basins reaches, 1980-2019. Flood events extracted above a 2-year return threshold. Validated against 6,000+ CONUS gauges (3-hourly) and 14,000+ gauges worldwide (daily). Citation confirmed: Yang, Pan, Lin, Beck, Zeng, Yamazaki, David, Lu, Yang, Hong, Wood, 2021, BAMS, doi:10.1175/BAMS-D-20-0057.1.
confirmed_sources.relevance: MEDIUM-HIGH. A modelled 1980-2019 discharge series for Periyar reaches - covers 2018 - usable as a prior or a sanity check, though it is model output, not gauge data.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes - resolution, span, reach count, 2-year threshold and the BAMS citation all confirmed

confirmed_sources.name: delta-HBV2 / delta-MC2 global streamflow (Nature Communications 2025 + Zenodo)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Paper: 'Distinct hydrologic response patterns and trends worldwide revealed by physics-embedded learning', Ji, Song, Bindas, Shen, Yang, Pan, Liu, Rahmani, Abbas, Beck, Lawson & Wada, Nature Communications 16, 9169, 15 Oct 2025. Quote: 'Once trained, deltaHBV2 can simulate runoff for around 2.94 million MERIT unit basins worldwide and then routes the runoff using a differentiable Muskingum-Cunge model.' Companion Zenodo record 20684429 confirmed: 'High-Resolution Global Streamflow Dataset from 1980 - 2020 for 2.94 Million Rivers Using the Physics-Embedded deltaHBV2-deltaMC2 Model', v5, 18 June 2026, 130.9 GB across 8 continental archives - South Asia is 21.8 GB, the one covering the Periyar.
confirmed_sources.relevance: MEDIUM. Gives you a differentiable-MC-routed discharge series over the Periyar for 1980-2020 without running anything.
confirmed_sources.http_status: 200 (nature.com, via auth redirect); DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-64367-1 200; Zenodo 20684429 = 403-bot-blocked to curl, confirmed 200 via WebFetch
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes - title, reach count, span, file size, continent split and licence all confirmed exactly
confirmed_sources.caveat: Licence is a Pennsylvania State University Non-Commercial Software License Agreement; commercial use needs 'prior written consent from PSU'. The record publishes discharge (plus unevaluated ET, soil moisture, SWE) and the description does NOT expose the learned Manning-n or channel-geometry parameters - so it does not directly solve AquaSync's K/x gap.
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Zenodo record 20684429, download the South Asia zip (21.8 GB) only

confirmed_sources.name: NOAA-OWP/inundation-mapping (HAND-FIM)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Confirmed verbatim: 'This software uses the Height Above Nearest Drainage (HAND) method to generate Relative Elevation Models (REMs), Synthetic Rating Curves (SRCs), and catchment grids', producing flood inundation maps from discharge.
confirmed_sources.relevance: MEDIUM as a METHOD reference for gap #4; LOW as a drop-in tool, for the reason below.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: partly - the HAND/REM/SRC/FIM pipeline is confirmed, but the prior sweep omitted the same lock-in objection it correctly raised against t-route
confirmed_sources.caveat: IMPORTANT OMISSION IN THE ORIGINAL WRITE-UP: this is hard-wired to US infrastructure. The README opens by saying it is 'configured to work with the U.S. National Water Model' and its inputs are US-specific - NHDPlusHR and the Watershed Boundary Dataset (WBD). Applying it to the Periyar would need substantial rework, exactly like t-route. Use pyflwdir to build HAND for Kerala instead and borrow only the synthetic-rating-curve idea from here.

confirmed_sources.name: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (AWS Open Data)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 'A Digital Surface Model (DSM) which represents the surface of the Earth including buildings, infrastructure and vegetation.' GLO-30 Public at 30 m, GLO-90 at 90 m worldwide. Anonymous S3 access confirmed: arn:aws:s3:::copernicus-dem-30m and copernicus-dem-90m in eu-central-1, readable with 'aws s3 ls --no-sign-request s3://copernicus-dem-30m/'.
confirmed_sources.relevance: HIGH. The licence-clean DEM baseline for a SFINCS Aluva/Kochi model - and unlike FABDEM it carries no non-commercial restriction.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: partly - DSM nature, resolutions, free access and no-sign-request S3 confirmed; the 'flattened water bodies, consistent river flow direction, edited shorelines' detail is standard Copernicus documentation but is not stated on this registry page
confirmed_sources.caveat: Two things to weigh. (1) GLO-30 Public is noted as having 'limited worldwide coverage' - verify the Periyar tiles exist before planning around it. (2) It is a DSM: buildings and vegetation are IN the surface, which will artificially block floodplain flow paths around Aluva. That is precisely the problem FABDEM was built to fix, so the prior sweep's framing of 'GLO-30 or FABDEM' as interchangeable is misleading - they trade licence freedom against bare-earth accuracy.
confirmed_sources.license: free for the general public under Copernicus DEM terms

confirmed_sources.name: FABDEM V1-2 (Forest And Buildings removed Copernicus DEM)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 'FABDEM (Forest And Buildings removed Copernicus DEM) is a global elevation map that removes building and tree height biases from the Copernicus GLO 30 Digital Elevation Model (DEM).' 1 arc-second (~30 m), global. A geojson of tiles ships with the dataset.
confirmed_sources.relevance: HIGH technically - bare-earth is what a floodplain model wants - but see the licence caveat, which may disqualify it depending on AquaSync's end use.
confirmed_sources.http_status: 200 (Bristol landing page); data.bris.ac.uk now returns 302 after ~25 s, i.e. slow/redirecting rather than the 000 previously reported; ERL paper DOI 10.1088/1748-9326/ac4d4f 200
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: partly - the product description is confirmed, but the licence was omitted entirely from the original write-up and it is the single most important fact about this source
confirmed_sources.caveat: LICENCE IS CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 - NON-COMMERCIAL AND SHARE-ALIKE. Quote: 'The FABDEM dataset is licensed under a Creative Commons CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license', with a contact address 'For commercial use queries'. A decision-support twin operated by or for KSEB (a state utility) is a licence question that needs answering before FABDEM goes anywhere near the pipeline. Actual data host is http://data.bris.ac.uk/data/dataset/s5hqmjcdj8yo2ibzi9b4ew3sn.
confirmed_sources.download_hint: data.bris.ac.uk dataset s5hqmjcdj8yo2ibzi9b4ew3sn; 10x10 degree zips of 1-degree tiles

confirmed_sources.name: GUARDIAN - sub-daily river discharge over India
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 'ExtendinG SUb-DAily River Discharge data over INdia (GUARDIAN)', Scientific Data, 18 Oct 2024. Extracts water-surface-elevation from 1,365 India-WRIS stations, fits rating curves with four algorithms (second-degree polynomial, exponential, quadratic, cubic), and keeps the 210 stations achieving 'Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) of more than 0.6'. Produces 'hourly discharge series during monsoon (June-September)' and sub-daily otherwise, 'from the year 2020 to the present', 'over 800,000 discharge data points' annually.
confirmed_sources.relevance: HIGH as METHOD VALIDATION. This is peer-reviewed precedent for exactly the stage-to-discharge rating-curve manoeuvre needed to recover the missing 2018-08-16..22 Periyar peak, including a defensible acceptance threshold (NSE >= 0.6).
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes - station count, resolution, start year, four algorithms, NSE threshold and annual point count all confirmed exactly
confirmed_sources.caveat: The paper does NOT specifically mention Kerala or the Periyar, so do not assume a ready-made Periyar rating curve exists in it. Its value here is the method and the QC threshold, not the data. Note also its monsoon-hourly / non-monsoon-sub-daily pattern independently explains the seasonal coverage I measured in the CWC stage file.

confirmed_sources.name: GHI / GHSA - Geospatial dataset for Hydrologic analyses in India
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Quality-controlled CWC/WRIS gauge metadata, catchment boundaries and hydrometeorological time series. Zenodo 13852439 confirmed: 'Geospatial dataset for hydrologic analyses within the Indian subcontinent (GHI): Version 2', published 27 Sept 2024, files ghi_v2409.zip (653.4 MB) + Readme.txt (8.0 kB), covering 'all 1677 stations' with delineated catchment boundaries.
confirmed_sources.relevance: MEDIUM-HIGH. Independent, vetted catchment boundaries for the Periyar gauges - useful for checking the CWC report's 4,033 km2 Neeleeswaram area and for area-scaling runoff.
confirmed_sources.http_status: 200 (ESSD paper); Zenodo 13852439 = 403-bot-blocked to curl, confirmed 200 via WebFetch
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes for v2 - title, date, filename, size and the 1,677-station count all confirmed exactly
confirmed_sources.caveat: Licence is CC BY 4.0 (permissive - better than FABDEM or MERIT Hydro for this project). The Zenodo page does not state the year range, so the '1950-2020' / GHSA '1950-2023' spans remain unconfirmed; the separate GHSA record (ghsa_v2504.zip, 784.3 MB, 1,702 stations) was not independently verified.

confirmed_sources.name: Global Flood Database v1 (2000-2018)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 'Maps for 913 flood events from 2000-2018', MODIS Terra/Aqua at 250 m, availability 2000-02-17 to 2018-12-10. Bands: flooded (maximum extent), duration, clear_views, clear_perc, jrc_perm_water. 'Can be filtered by date, country, or Dartmouth Flood Observatory original ID.'

confirmed_sources.name: anuga-community/anuga_core (ANUGA)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Finite-volume unstructured-triangle 2D shallow water solver for dam-break, riverine and tsunami inundation; Python with C kernels.
confirmed_sources.relevance: MEDIUM. A genuine open-source alternative to SFINCS with true unstructured meshes; heavier to set up, but pip-installable.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: partly - the repo is real and active, but the provenance needs stating
confirmed_sources.caveat: REPO PROVENANCE: anuga-community/anuga_core is flagged fork=true by the GitHub API (parent stoiver/anuga_core, ultimate source GeoscienceAustralia/anuga_core). The upstream GeoscienceAustralia/anuga_core has more stars (227 vs 53) but is less active (pushed 2026-06-22 vs 2026-08-26). anuga-community is the live development line and is what the docs and PyPI track - so it is the right one to use, but cite it knowingly. Licence resolves as NOASSERTION on both, so check the LICENSE file before redistribution.
confirmed_sources.license: NOASSERTION per GitHub API - verify in-repo

confirmed_sources.name: open TELEMAC-MASCARET
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: TELEMAC-2D solves the depth-averaged Saint-Venant equations on unstructured meshes; consortium-governed open source.
confirmed_sources.relevance: LOW-MEDIUM for AquaSync. Powerful but by far the heaviest lift of the 2D options; hard to justify against SFINCS for this use case.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: partly - the site is live and is the official download page, but I could not read its content: the server presents an INCOMPLETE TLS CERTIFICATE CHAIN (missing Sectigo intermediate), so WebFetch fails with 'unable to verify the first certificate' while curl -L still returns 200
confirmed_sources.caveat: The cert-chain defect means the specific version and licence claims are UNVERIFIED. Do not quote a TELEMAC version number without checking in a browser first.

confirmed_sources.name: HydroSHEDS / HydroRIVERS
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Global river network line shapefiles at 15 arc-second resolution, distributed by continent, with HydroBASINS catchments and HydroATLAS attributes alongside.
confirmed_sources.relevance: MEDIUM. A second, independent vector network to cross-check MERIT-Basins topology on the Periyar/Chalakudy confluence - which matters a lot given the ARANGALI finding.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: partly - URL confirmed live and is the correct HydroRIVERS product page, but I did not deep-verify the resolution and distribution claims against page content
confirmed_sources.caveat: Lower-confidence entry: status-checked only, not content-audited. Treat the 15 arc-second figure as unconfirmed by me.

confirmed_sources.name: jsosa/LFPtools
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: CLI tools to prepare LISFLOOD-FP inputs from global data. I listed the repo's bin/ directory and confirmed every claimed tool exists plus more: lfp-getdepths, lfp-getwidths, lfp-getbankelevs, lfp-fixelevs, lfp-prepdata, and also lfp-buildmodel, lfp-getbedelevs, lfp-getdischarge, lfp-getinflows, lfp-getrunoff, lfp-getslopes, lfp-rasterresample, lfp-split.
confirmed_sources.relevance: LOW. Only useful if you commit to LISFLOOD-FP over SFINCS, and the staleness makes that a poor bet.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: partly - the CLI tool names are confirmed exactly, but the '1 km Severn model in 1.45 minutes' performance claim is from the paper and I did not verify it
confirmed_sources.caveat: EFFECTIVELY ABANDONED: last push 2021-04-19, over five years ago. Also a licence contradiction - the GitHub API reports BSD-3-Clause while setup.py declares MIT. It builds Cython extensions against the numpy C API (prepdata_utils.pyx), which is very likely to fail against modern numpy 2.x without patching. Budget real time for the build or skip it.
confirmed_sources.license: BSD-3-Clause per GitHub API, MIT per setup.py - inconsistent

confirmed_sources.name: mhpi/dMC-Juniata-hydroDL2 (differentiable Muskingum-Cunge)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: PyTorch + Hydra implementation of Bindas et al. 2024 WRR: Muskingum-Cunge with an embedded neural net mapping reach attributes to Manning's n and channel geometry, trained on downstream hydrographs only.
confirmed_sources.relevance: MEDIUM as the conceptual answer to gap #2 - learning routing parameters from downstream hydrographs is exactly the shape of AquaSync's problem, and Neeleeswaram is exactly such a downstream hydrograph. LOW as usable code.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes - and the 'research-only' characterisation is fair
confirmed_sources.caveat: Confirmed as paper-replication rather than a library: 11 stars, last push 2024-04-14 (over two years), ZERO open issues and zero PRs, 6 forks, repo contains only dMC/, notebooks/, environment.yml, requirements.txt. Licence CC-BY-4.0 is a documentation licence, not a software licence - awkward for reuse. The living successor DeepGroundwater/ddr (Apache-2.0, 11 stars, pushed 2026-08-19) is confirmed real and is the better starting point.

confirmed_sources.name: DeepGroundwater/ddr (Distributed Differentiable Routing)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The actively maintained successor line to dMC-Juniata for differentiable routing.
confirmed_sources.relevance: MEDIUM. If AquaSync pursues learned routing parameters, this is the maintained codebase to build on rather than the frozen dMC-Juniata.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes - existence, licence, stars and activity confirmed via API
confirmed_sources.caveat: Small project (11 stars). I confirmed its metadata but did not audit its README or API surface, so treat capability claims as unverified.

confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Spatially distributed rainfall-runoff-routing model in Python, requiring PCRaster and GDAL. Repo topics include 'efas', 'glofas', 'hydrological-modelling' and 'flood-forecasting'.

confirmed_sources.name: ISRO Bhoonidhi (NRSC) - registration portal
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Confirmed to be the genuine NRSC/ISRO Bhoonidhi registration page. Form collects name, user ID, password, country, user type (Academic / Private / Central Government / State government / DOS NRSC) and organisation, and references an 'END USER LICENCE AGREEMENT FOR USE OF REMOTE SENSING DATA'.
confirmed_sources.relevance: POTENTIALLY HIGH but UNPROVEN. An Indian national DEM would be the natural DEM for an Indian basin - but nothing on this page substantiates that CartoDEM is available here, at what resolution, or at what price.

Also unverified: whether the '1/3 arc-sec source subsampled to 1 and 3 arc-sec' description is accurate, and whether non-Indian users face different terms. Given a Copernicus GLO-30 tile is one anonymous S3 command away, treat Bhoonidhi as an optional upgrade, not a dependency.

rejected.name: HEC-RAS (USACE) downloads
rejected.reason: UNVERIFIABLE FROM HERE, AND THE VERSION CLAIMS ARE HALLUCINATION-SHAPED. I retried three URLs on the domain (the download page, the HEC-RAS product page, and the site root) and every one returned 000 - the entire hec.usace.army.mil host is unreachable from this network, so this is a block rather than a dead link. That means I could not confirm ANY of the specific claims: release 7.0.1 dated 2026-06-02, a ~171 MB setup, or a 'HEC-RAS 2025 Beta 0.1.0.2965 patch issued 2026-04-17'. Those are exactly the kind of precise-but-uncheckable details the project context warns about, and a build number like 0.1.0.2965 attached to a beta labelled '2025' issued in 2026 is internally odd. Note also it is Windows-only and not open source, so it sits outside this sweep's stated dimension anyway.

rejected.name: Iber (+ IberSWMM+)
rejected.reason: NOT OPEN SOURCE - fails the dimension - AND TWO KEY CLAIMS UNCONFIRMED. The URL resolves 200 and Iber is a real, capable 2D model, but its own download page states the licence terms as 'The reproduction, redistribution, public communication and processing of the software are strictly prohibited'. It is a free-to-download CLOSED-SOURCE binary requiring registration at iberaula.com, which disqualifies it from an 'open-source river routing, hydraulics and 2D flood inundation' list. Separately, neither of the two specific technical claims appears anywhere on the page I fetched: there is NO mention of a C++/OpenMP/CUDA GPU build or a ~200x speedup, and NO mention of IberSWMM, IberSWMM+, EPA SWMM coupling, or a J. Hydrology 2025 paper. The page does document modules I can see (hydrodynamics, water quality, plus new v3 IBER-WOOD large-wood and IBER-NNF non-Newtonian modules), so the tool is genuine - but the write-up's two headline specifics are unsupported and should not be repeated.

verification_notes: BIGGEST CORRECTION - THE MUSKINGUM HEADLINE IS WRONG. The claim that 'two gauges on one river with synchronous hourly stage is exactly the input a Muskingum K/x fit needs' does not survive. The CWC file's OWN metadata settles it: ARANGALI has Tributary=Chalakudy, Local River=Chalakudy, District=THRISSUR. It is on the Chalakudy, which joins the Periyar DOWNSTREAM of Neeleeswaram - so the two gauges are on different rivers and are not an inflow/outflow pair. The prior agent hedged ('confirm topology against MERIT-Basins') but then led with the pair anyway; no MERIT-Basins check was needed, the answer was two columns to the right in the file already downloaded. I enumerated every Periyar/Chalakudy station in basin 031: the ONLY true Periyar-mainstem river gauges are VANDIPERIYAR (9.573N, 77.091E, upper basin) and NEELEESWARAM (10.184N, 76.496E, below both dams) - and Mullaperiyar's inter-basin diversion, Idukki and Idamalayar all sit between them, so that pair is not an unregulated channel reach either. GAP #2 IS NOT CLOSED BY THIS DATA AS DESCRIBED.

THE SALVAGE, AND IT IS STILL GOOD. There IS a defensible Muskingum reach here, just not the claimed one: dam outflow (Idukki spill + powerhouse, plus Idamalayar spill) routed down to NEELEESWARAM. That is precisely the reach AquaSync cares about (dams to Aluva). For August 2018 the upstream boundary comes from the CWC report's hourly Idukki/Idamalayar operation narrative and Fig.4, and the downstream boundary is the confirmed 100%-complete hourly Neeleeswaram stage. ARANGALI is not wasted either - as a Chalakudy gauge it is the lateral-inflow boundary for the Periyar below Neeleeswaram, which is exactly what a downstream Aluva/Kochi inundation model needs. Reframe, do not discard.

THE UNDERLYING DATA CLAIMS ARE EXCEPTIONALLY SOLID - I could not break them. I re-parsed both cached CSVs with my own script and every row count reproduced EXACTLY: 1,284,651 and 1,139,984 total; NEELEESWARAM 31,172+25,643; ARANGALI 30,186+27,460; VANDIPERIYAR 48,949+26,714; Idukki 3,532+9,477; Idamalayar 3,621+9,561. Individual values matched too: Neeleeswaram 6.12 m at 2018-08-14 00:00 and 12.40 m first reached 2018-08-16 16:00; Idukki 722.31/728.69 m and Idamalayar 152.58/164.23 m at the two claimed stamps. The discharge file reproduced exactly as well: 217,538 rows, 40 stations, NEELEESWARAM 8,478 values, record max 6,323.5474 on 2013-08-05, 2018-08-15 = 6,166.426, 2021-10-12 = 1,387.14, 2021-10-09 = 695.46. This is verified, reproducible fact, not a plausible-sounding list - a genuinely strong result for gap #1.

THE CORRUPT-WINDOW REPAIR CLAIM IS OVERSTATED BY ROUGHLY HALF. 'Spans the corrupt 2020-09-25 -> 2021-04-30 window' is not true. The reservoir series runs 2019-06-10 to 2020-12-31 and then JUMPS to 2021-05-12 - a four-and-a-half month hole. It supplies 881 (Idukki) / 882 (Idamalayar) readings inside the corrupt window, all of them at or before 2020-12-31 22:00, and NOTHING for 2021-01-01 to 2021-04-30. So CWC can repair the Sept-Dec 2020 portion of the amith-vp corruption and none of the Jan-Apr 2021 portion. The '14 months before amith-vp' part is correct and stands.

STAGE COVERAGE IS SEASONAL, NOT CONTINUOUS HOURLY - which is fine, but plan for it. NEELEESWARAM 2018 monthly completeness measured against unique timestamps: Aug 100%, Jul 98%, Oct 89%, Sep 87%, Jun 84%, Nov 69%, but only 11-15% for Dec-May. So '31,172 hourly stage readings 2015-06-01 to 2020-12-31' is literally true but reads as continuous when it is monsoon-hourly and dry-season-sparse. Happily this lands where it matters: August 2018 is 743 of 744 hours, and October 2021 is a perfect 744 of 744. Idukki and Idamalayar in Oct 2021 are much thinner at 38% (280 and 279 of 744 hours) - still an independent validator for the flagship replay, just not the ~3-hourly-throughout implied.

UNDOCUMENTED DATA-QUALITY LANDMINE: DUPLICATE AND CONFLICTING TIMESTAMPS. In the 1991-2020 file, NEELEESWARAM has 31,172 rows but only 29,835 unique timestamps - 1,337 duplicate rows, and 667 of those timestamps carry CONFLICTING values (e.g. 2018-08-11 08:00 appears as both 6.84 and 6.80). The 2021-2025 file is clean (zero duplicates). Any least-squares K/x fit or rating-curve regression must deduplicate first or it will silently double-weight ~4% of the 2015-2020 record and ingest contradictory pairs. This was not mentioned at all. Separately, VANDIPERIYAR mixes datums - RL_of_zeroGauge is 789.0 m and values range 1.88 to 797.3, i.e. some rows are gauge height and some are reduced level - so it needs unit triage before any use.

LICENCE RESTRICTIONS WERE OMITTED ACROSS THE BOARD, AND THEY MATTER FOR A KSEB/KSDMA HANDOFF. FABDEM is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 - explicitly NON-COMMERCIAL and share-alike. MERIT Hydro is dual CC BY-NC 4.0 / ODbL 1.0, where the commercial option forces derived data to be published under ODbL share-alike. The delta-HBV2 Zenodo dataset carries a Penn State Non-Commercial Software License needing written PSU consent for commercial use. SFINCS is GPL-3.0 in source but its precompiled Windows exe is Deltares Freeware with 'no distribution, no modification'. None of this was flagged. The licence-clean alternatives are Copernicus GLO-30 (free, anonymous S3) and GHI (CC BY 4.0). Note the real trade-off the write-up flattened: GLO-30 is a DSM including buildings and vegetation, which will falsely dam floodplain flow paths around Aluva - that is exactly the defect FABDEM exists to fix, so 'GLO-30 or FABDEM' are not interchangeable, they trade licence freedom against bare-earth accuracy.

THE US-LOCK-IN OBJECTION WAS APPLIED TO t-route BUT NOT TO inundation-mapping, THOUGH IT APPLIES EQUALLY. The t-route assessment is accurate and I confirmed it verbatim ('bespoke for NWM', WSL required on Windows, gfortran + netcdf-fortran + compiler.sh, master frozen since 2025-01-31 despite a 2026-08-18 pushed_at). But NOAA-OWP/inundation-mapping is described as an operational continental-scale HAND-FIM framework with no such caveat, when its README states it is 'configured to work with the U.S. National Water Model' and its inputs are NHDPlusHR and the US Watershed Boundary Dataset. Same rework burden, no warning. For Kerala, build HAND with pyflwdir (confirmed to provide HAND and geomorphic floodplain delineation verbatim) and borrow only the synthetic-rating-curve concept from the NOAA repo.

TWO CITATIONS I EXPECTED TO BE FABRICATED TURNED OUT REAL - worth recording so they are not needlessly dropped. (1) 'GMD 18, 9827, 2025' for LISFLOOD-FP 8.2 resolves 200 and is genuinely Chowdhury & Kesserwani, 'LISFLOOD-FP 8.2: GPU-accelerated multiwavelet discontinuous Galerkin solver with dynamic resolution adaptivity', GMD 18(23), 9827-9854, 10 Dec 2025 - even though the seamlesswave page itself cites a different paper (Advances in Water Resources 201C, 104986). Both exist. (2) The Nature Communications paper is real and says what was claimed: Ji et al., 'Distinct hydrologic response patterns and trends worldwide revealed by physics-embedded learning', Nat Commun 16, 9169, 15 Oct 2025, quote 'can simulate runoff for around 2.94 million MERIT unit basins worldwide and then routes the runoff using a differentiable Muskingum-Cunge model'. Zenodo 20684429 v5 (2026-06-18, 130.9 GB, South Asia zip 21.8 GB) confirmed. Note Zenodo returns 403 to curl from this IP but resolves fine via WebFetch - bot blocking, not a dead record.

TOOLING VERDICT AFTER ADVERSARIAL CHECK: the SFINCS recommendation survives and is the right call for gap #4. SFINCS-LIE/SFINCS-SSWE naming, GPL-3.0 source, the Windows exe at download.deltares.nl/sfincs, the deltares/sfincs-cpu Docker image, release v2.4.0_Galibier 2026-06-15, and hydromt_sfincs (GPL-3.0, 35 stars, PyPI 1.2.2 on 2025-12-02) all confirmed. Pair it with pyflwdir (MIT, 116 stars, pushed 2026-08-25, full feature list confirmed word-for-word) for DEM conditioning and HAND, and Copernicus GLO-30 for a licence-clean DEM. river-route's four-column parquet spec (river_id, downstream_river_id, k, x; -1 for outlets; topologically sorted) is confirmed VERBATIM and its lack of a calibrator is confirmed too - so it is a reference implementation, not the answer to gap #2. One dimension-level gap remains unaddressed by this whole sweep: NOTHING here touches gap #3, the perfect-foresight assumption in the optimiser, which the project context names as the biggest weakness. Routing and inundation tools cannot fix a forecasting problem.
